name: Parque Ibirapuera
desc: São Paulo's green lung: lakes, museums, joggers, capybara rumors. A full free Sunday, batteries included.

name: Avenida Paulista
desc: On Sundays the skyscraper canyon closes to cars and fills with buskers and dogs in sweaters. Peak free Sampa.

name: MASP
desc: The red-legged icon floating over Paulista, paintings hung on glass like they levitate. Save up, then linger for hours.

name: Mercadão Municipal
desc: Stained-glass market famous for absurd mortadella sandwiches and fruit sellers who insist you try everything.

name: Beco do Batman
desc: An open-air alley gallery in Vila Madalena where the murals change before your feed does. Zero reais, all color.

name: Bairro da Liberdade
desc: Red lanterns over the largest Japanese community outside Japan. Window-shop snacks now, feast someday.

name: Pinacoteca de São Paulo
desc: Brazilian art in a sunlit brick palace by the old train station. Six bucks, and free some days if you time it right.

name: Farol Santander
desc: Ride up an old bank tower to watch the city's endless skyline blur into the horizon. Vertigo, but make it romantic.

name: Catedral da Sé
desc: A huge neo-gothic cathedral at kilometer zero of the megacity. Free to enter, impossible to fit in one photo.

name: Theatro Municipal
desc: A gilded opera house straight out of Paris envy. Tours cost pocket change; the chandelier gawking is free with it.
